summary: Proposes four cryptographic suites for IPsec that are compatible with the US National Security Agency's Suite B specifications, similar to the two suites in RFC 4308. It obsoletes RFC 4869 and is now historic.

eli5.summary: Instead of picking each secret-code setting one at a time, you choose a ready-made bundle. This offers four such bundles matching a government set of rules. It is historic.

questions: what are the suite b gcm and gmac suites
what is a ipsec ui suite
subtitle: Four ready-made IPsec option bundles that line up with the NSA's Suite B algorithms.

tldr.problem: IPsec has many cryptographic options, and two peers need to agree on a matching set. Users who want the algorithms of the US National Security Agency's Suite B need a simple, named way to ask for them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines four named user interface suites, Suite-B-GCM-128, Suite-B-GCM-256, Suite-B-GMAC-128 and Suite-B-GMAC-256. Each fixes the algorithms for ESP and for IKEv2.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 4869 and is now Historic. The suites are only collections of option values and do not change the IPsec protocols.

today: RFC 6379 is Historic. It obsoleted RFC 4869, and the text points to RFC 6380 for the IKE authentication methods that were removed from the suite definitions.

sections.title: Introduction and Purpose
sections.content:
RFC 4308 proposed two optional cryptographic user interface suites (UI suites) for IPsec, named VPN-A and VPN-B. RFC 4869 then proposed four suites based on the United States National Security Agency's Suite B algorithms.

As with the VPN suites, these are simply collections of values for some options in IPsec. Using a UI suite does not change the IPsec protocols in any way. This document reduces the scope of the suites in RFC 4869 while keeping the original suite names, and it obsoletes RFC 4869.
sections.eli5: A suite is a menu combo: instead of ordering each dish separately, you pick one set. The combo does not change how the kitchen cooks.

sections.title: The Four Suites
sections.content:
Each suite gives choices for ESP (the Encapsulating Security Payload) and for the Internet Key Exchange, IKEv2. The four suites differ in two ways: the strength of the algorithms, and whether ESP provides both confidentiality and integrity or integrity only. The names come from the AES mode and AES key length chosen for ESP.

  • Suite-B-GCM-128 and Suite-B-GCM-256 give ESP integrity protection and confidentiality using AES-GCM with 128-bit or 256-bit keys. They are for when both are needed.
  • Suite-B-GMAC-128 and Suite-B-GMAC-256 give ESP integrity protection only, using AES-GMAC, with no confidentiality. They should be used only when there is no need for ESP encryption.

Implementations that use these suites MUST use these names. They SHOULD NOT use different names for the suites described here, and MUST NOT use these names for suites that do not match these values. This is needed for interoperability.
sections.eli5: There are four combos: two that lock the message and check it, and two that only check it was not changed. Each comes in a medium-strong and a stronger size.

sections.title: Algorithm Choices in Each Suite
sections.content:
The 128-bit suites use AES with 128-bit keys. For IKEv2 they use AES in CBC mode, HMAC-SHA-256 as the pseudo-random function, HMAC-SHA-256-128 for integrity, and a 256-bit random ECP Diffie-Hellman group.

The 256-bit suites use AES with 256-bit keys, HMAC-SHA-384 as the pseudo-random function, HMAC-SHA-384-192 for integrity and a 384-bit random ECP group.

For ESP, the GCM suites use AES-GCM with a 16-octet integrity check value and NULL as the separate integrity algorithm. The GMAC suites use NULL encryption and AES in GMAC mode for integrity.
sections.eli5: Each combo lists exactly which lock, which fingerprint check and which secret-handshake size to use, so both sides pick the same ones.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The document inherits all of the security considerations of the IPsec and IKEv2 documents. It also warns that some of the security options in these suites may in the future be found to have properties significantly weaker than those believed at the time of writing.

IANA keeps a registry called "Cryptographic Suites for IKEv1, IKEv2, and IPsec". The four suite identifiers are listed with RFC 6379 as the reference.
sections.eli5: Today's strong lock might turn out weaker later, so the authors say so. The four combo names are written in an official list.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 4869
sections.content:
Compared with RFC 4869 there are three changes:

  • The definitions of the suites for IKEv1 were removed.
  • The IKE authentication methods were removed from the suite definitions. They now appear in RFC 6380.
  • The requirements on rekeying in IKEv2 were removed.
sections.eli5: The new version trimmed the old menu: it dropped some items that now live in another document.
